title: SSE orchestration: hybrid fragment validation and reconnect negotiation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a robust SSE (Server-Sent Events) orchestration layer that performs deterministic fragment validation, preserves tool/function-call boundaries for structured outputs, and negotiates reconnect behavior with backward-compatible fallbacks for older clients. This ticket covers protocol design changes, runtime validation, client/server handshake extensions, end-to-end tests, and a staged rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: SSE fragments carry a compact validation header (fragment-id, seq, checksum) and runtime validates header before reassembly
Function call frames are atomically preserved across fragmentation — no toolcall JSON partial emission on reconnects
Reconnect negotiation protocol supports both optimistic resume (resume-token) and conservative replay (offset-based) with server-declared compatibility flag
Clients that do not understand the new header can fall back to existing JSONL boundary heuristics without breaking existing sessions
Automated e2e tests that simulate mid-stream disconnects validate no duplication, no loss of toolcall boundaries, and correct structured-output reassembly
Telemetry surfaced in Console: per-session resume attempts, successful resume rate, fragment validation failures, and reconstructed-output latency
arch_decisions: Use a short binary-safe fragment header (base64-encoded in SSE event field) instead of embedding long JSON metadata to minimize token overhead
Treat tool/function calls as first-class frames: begin_call and end_call markers are emitted with fragment lineage metadata to allow atomic reassembly
Server prefers optimistic resume when KV-cache TTL indicates available state; otherwise falls back to replay to guarantee deterministic outputs
Maintain a compatibility bit in the session handshake so older clients are routed to an emulation codepath that preserves JSONL boundaries
progress_updates: 2025-02-18: Drafted initial design and shared with runtime team. Identified need to change per-chunk header format to include 16-bit seq and 64-bit fragment-id.
2025-02-24: Prototype header encoder/decoder implemented in runtime branch runtime/sse-frag-header. Simple base64 envelope validated in local harness.

2025-02-27: Experimented with preserving functioncall boundaries by emitting begin_call/end_call sentinel events. Observed mid-stream reconnect produced duplicate end_call under optimistic resume — created mitigation plan (idempotent-call-guard).
2025-03-03: Added reconnect negotiation flags: resume-token, resume-window, compatibility-bit. Backend now emits compatibility=false for older model instances until feature rollout.

2025-03-05: Integration tests added to CI that simulate reconnects with out-of-order fragments and partial toolcall fragments. Current failure rate reduced to 1.2% from 7% after idempotent-call-guard fix.
tests: integration: reconnect negotiation matrix (client v1, v2, v3 x server compat true/false x optimistic/replay)
e2e: real model serving with KV cache enabled; simulate TCP drop at token 512 and verify reconstructed JSON output matches pre-drop golden
fuzz: random fragmentation and out-of-order delivery against JSONL and nested functioncall payloads
rollout_plan: feature-flag gate: enable new fragment header on 1% of sessions - metric: fragment_validation_fail_rate
increase to 10% after 48h if fail_rate < 0.5% and resume_success_rate >= 98%
enable default for hosted API and Dedicated green pools after 2 weeks and manual check of toolcall integrity dashboards
private deployments: provide opt-in config and migration guide; require KMS-backed token store before enabling optimistic resume
migration_notes: Provide client SDK patches for Node/Python that parse the header and expose a `session.resume()` helper
Compatibility shim will continue to emit JSONL events for clients that declare legacy=true in the handshake
Update Console trace viewer to show fragment lineage with hoverable checksums and reconstructed boundaries
risks: Increased per-fragment overhead could slightly raise p50 token latency under high QPS if header handling is not optimized in C++ hot path
Edge cases where fragments are lost from multiple consecutive segments may force full replay causing higher cost
Clients that ignore idempotency guards could replay toolcalls if they re-emit requests — need SDKs to prevent accidental re-invocations
mitigations: Implement header parsing in native runtime via SIMD-friendly path and minimize allocations
Expose server-declared resume_window to clients so SDKs can apply backoff and avoid aggressive resume attempts
Add server-side idempotent-call-guard that deduplicates toolcall side-effects by request-sig if functioncall metadata is present
